build-drag.reason: Placing widgets by drag is the core job of a dashboard builder; all five competitors have it.

build-resize.reason: Sizing widgets is part of building a dashboard at all; the demo is not convincing without it.

build-keyboard.reason: Accessibility requirement: a government organisation cannot use a layout editor that needs a mouse.

build-columns.reason: Organisations adjust the grid to their content; two competitors have it, a setting one organisation will change.

build-responsive.reason: Table stakes: four of five competitors reflow for narrow screens, and staff open the start page on phones.

build-container.reason: Three of five competitors group widgets; a real start page needs sections to stay readable.

build-style.reason: Only one competitor rates yes; per widget colours are polish, not needed to do the job.

build-picker.reason: Choosing a widget to add is part of the one flow the app exists for.

build-nc-widgets.reason: Showing other Nextcloud apps' widgets is the reason to use a start page inside Nextcloud.

build-no-overlap.reason: Three of five competitors place new widgets in a free spot; without it daily editing is frustrating.

build-edit-lock.reason: Concurrent editing of shared dashboards matters at scale with many editors; no competitor rates yes, so not table stakes.

build-personal-hide.reason: Two competitors have it, and staff on a shared group dashboard need to hide widgets they do not use.

build-config-file.reason: Deferred: one competitor yes and no demand; export and import already cover moving dashboards.

build-rollback.reason: Restoring an earlier version is hardening for organisations with many shared dashboards; no competitor rates yes.

dash-many.reason: Personal and team dashboards side by side is the core idea; switching between them must be shown.

dash-default.reason: Three competitors let users choose which dashboard opens first; needed once people have more than one.

dash-describe.reason: Two competitors have it; titles and icons are needed to tell dashboards apart in daily use.

dash-copy.reason: Only one competitor rates yes; starting from a template or empty dashboard covers the need.

dash-link.reason: Three competitors support direct links; organisations link dashboards from mail and the intranet.

dash-shared-list.reason: Once dashboards are shared, people need one place to find them; one competitor yes.

dash-tree.reason: No competitor rates yes; a page tree is intranet structure outside the core start page job.

dash-empty.reason: A first run offer to create a dashboard keeps new users from a blank page; one competitor yes.

dash-languages.reason: Multilingual content is a demand of larger and border region organisations; two competitors have it.

dash-metadata.reason: No competitor rates yes and no demand row; recording an owning department is administrative extra.

dash-starter-widgets.reason: A new dashboard with useful widgets is what makes the first demo work without manual setup.

d-start-full-width.reason: A layout setting an administrator of one organisation will want to change; no competitor data.

tile-pin.reason: Launching apps and sites from tiles is the start page half of the core job; four competitors have it.

tile-health.reason: Two self hosted competitors rate yes; service status is a homelab need more than an office one.

tile-filter.reason: Two competitors rate yes; useful only on dashboards with many tiles.

tile-web-search.reason: Two homelab competitors rate yes; organisations already have browser search.

tile-bookmarks.reason: Three competitors have grouped link lists; a common start page need for every organisation.

tile-clicks.reason: Usage reporting on tiles serves administrators of larger rollouts; one competitor rates yes.

tile-most-used.reason: Two competitors rate yes; automatic ordering is convenience, not needed for the job.

tile-legacy-apps.reason: Digital workplace tenders such as Almelo name Workspace 365 for this; it wins tenders, not daily use.

tile-local-apps.reason: Only Workspace 365 rates yes; starting local programs is outside a browser start page.

tile-sso-app.reason: Single sign on into company apps is an integration Workspace 365 sells to tender buyers.

tile-catalogue.reason: An approved app catalogue with requests is an IT governance feature for larger organisations; one competitor yes.

tile-discover-containers.reason: Only Homarr rates yes; a homelab feature with no organisational demand.

tile-org-nav.reason: Three competitors offer an organisation wide menu; an organisation needs it beside every dashboard.

w-text.reason: Formatted text is the simplest widget and needed to show any content in the demo.

w-image.reason: Three competitors have image widgets; an organisation's start page needs pictures.

w-video.reason: Two competitors rate yes; video on a start page is occasional.

w-embed.reason: Only Workspace 365 rates yes; useful but organisations can link instead of embedding.

w-news.reason: Table stakes: four of five competitors show news feeds on the start page.

w-weather.reason: Three competitors rate yes, but all are homelab or Nextcloud; organisations rarely need weather.

w-clock.reason: Two homelab competitors rate yes; not needed for an organisation's start page.

w-calendar.reason: Three competitors show upcoming events; seeing today's agenda is daily start page use.

w-files.reason: Files is the centre of Nextcloud; all competitors partial, and staff expect their folders here.

w-people.reason: No competitor fully rates yes; colleague lists are intranet extras.

w-birthdays.reason: Only Workspace 365 rates yes; a social extra with no demand.

w-structure.reason: One competitor rates yes; headings help layout but text widgets cover the need.

w-action-button.reason: Two competitors rate yes; one click actions are convenience on top of tiles.

w-live-value.reason: Three competitors show live figures; organisations use it for queue counts and status values.

w-charts.reason: Charts over registered data is reporting, a production concern; no competitor fully rates yes.

w-bi-embed.reason: Deferred: partial, built, no demand; only Workspace 365 rates yes.

w-spend.reason: Finance figures across fleet apps is an integration for reporting; no competitor rates yes.

w-scheduled-export.reason: Scheduled reports by mail is reporting demand at scale; no competitor data yet.

w-cross-filter.reason: No competitor data and no demand; analytics behaviour beyond a start page.

int-builder.reason: A no code connector to business systems is an integration Workspace 365 sells in tenders.

int-itsm.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

int-erp.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

int-mail.reason: Mailbox preview is an integration with the mail app; only Workspace 365 rates yes.

int-tasks.reason: Task integration with planning apps; two competitors rate yes, needed for digital workplace tenders.

int-office-tiles.reason: Ready made office suite tiles are an integration two intranet competitors sell.

int-intranet-content.reason: Showing another intranet's content is integration work two competitors offer.

int-connections-status.reason: Connection status is operational hardening once outside integrations are in use.

t-groups.reason: Showing widgets per group is the smart visibility the app promises; four competitors have some form.

t-hours.reason: No competitor rates yes; time windows are a refinement of group targeting.

t-dates.reason: No competitor rates yes; date windows help campaigns but are not daily need.

t-attribute.reason: Targeting by profile field is fine grained admin; one competitor yes, useful for large organisations.

t-preview.reason: Previewing who sees a widget is admin tooling for complex rule sets; one competitor yes.

t-overview.reason: An overview of all visibility rules is fine grained admin at scale; no competitor rates yes.

t-widget-kinds.reason: Restricting widget kinds per group is fine grained admin; no competitor fully rates yes.

t-role-layout.reason: A starting layout per role is how one organisation sets up its staff; competitors partial.

t-device.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

t-hide-incompatible.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

t-group-priority.reason: Needed once group dashboards exist and people belong to several groups; two competitors have it.

t-action-matrix.reason: A role by action grid is fine grained admin; two competitors rate yes.

r-templates.reason: Rolling a dashboard out to groups is the team half of the core job; two competitors have it.

r-permission-levels.reason: One competitor rates yes; an organisation must decide who may change a handed out dashboard.

r-resync.reason: Pushing template changes to existing dashboards matters with many users; no competitor fully rates yes.

r-group-dashboards.reason: A shared dashboard per group beside personal ones is the team dashboard the app exists for.

r-wizard.reason: Guided setup helps one organisation get started without consultancy; one competitor rates yes.

r-demo.reason: Example dashboards are the demo data that makes the core flow demonstrable.

r-report-gallery.reason: No competitor data and no demand; a report gallery is analytics outside the core job.

r-delegate.reason: Table stakes: four competitors let non admins manage dashboards, needed in daily operation.

r-bulk.reason: Bulk changes matter only at scale with many dashboards; no competitor rates yes.

r-export.reason: Export and import between servers is migration, a production concern; one competitor yes.

r-migrate-from.reason: Decided no: no competitor rates yes, no demand, outside the core area.

r-confluence.reason: Importing Confluence content is migration work for organisations switching; no competitor fully rates yes.

r-registry.reason: No competitor rates yes and the end to end flow is unverified; sharing between organisations is extra.

r-quota.reason: Quotas protect a large installation from misuse; no competitor rates yes.

r-personal-off.reason: Table stakes: four competitors let an organisation turn off personal dashboards.

s-share.reason: Sharing with people and groups is basic team use; three competitors rate yes.

s-public.reason: Two competitors offer public read only links; organisations publish dashboards to outsiders.

s-public-protect.reason: Password and expiry on public links is security hardening; no competitor rates yes.

s-bruteforce.reason: Throttling password guesses is security hardening expected in tenders; no competitor rates yes.

s-notify.reason: People must learn that a dashboard was shared with them; a basic part of sharing.

s-kiosk.reason: No competitor fully rates yes and no demand row; lobby screens are a niche use.

s-schedule.reason: No competitor rates yes and no demand row; built because Ruben decided so, not because buyers ask.

s-policy.reason: Deciding who may share with whom is fine grained admin for larger organisations; no competitor rates yes.

s-leaver.reason: Handing over dashboards of leavers matters at scale; no competitor rates yes.

s-discussion.reason: No competitor data and no demand; Talk already covers discussion.

s-omnichannel.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

e-ack-ask.reason: No competitor rates yes and no demand row; built on Ruben's decision, not buyer demand.

e-ack-report.reason: Depends on read confirmations, which have no competitor yes and no demand.

e-react.reason: No competitor rates yes and no demand row; emoji reactions are engagement extra.

e-announcements.reason: Targeted news with comments is an intranet suite feature Workspace 365 and Viva bring to tenders.

e-events.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

e-kb.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

e-communities.reason: Two intranet competitors rate yes, but communities sit outside the start page job.

e-digest.reason: Two competitors rate yes; an email digest is convenience beyond the core job.

e-activity-stream.reason: Decided no: the personal activity stream is the Nextcloud activity app.

e-maintenance.reason: Two competitors have it; an organisation needs to warn everyone about outages.

a-find-dashboard.reason: Two competitors support search; finding dashboards from the Nextcloud search bar is basic navigation.

a-federated.reason: Decided no: unified search is provided by Nextcloud server.

a-assistant.reason: Only Workspace 365 rates yes and no demand row; built on Ruben's decision.

a-place-widget.reason: No competitor rates yes and no demand; AI placement is a convenience.

a-agent-tools.reason: One competitor rates yes and no demand; an AI tool surface is extra.

a-ai-control.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

a-summarise.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

g-views.reason: View statistics with export are reporting for administrators of larger rollouts; one competitor yes.

g-optout.reason: Deferred: built, no demand; only needed with view tracking.

g-health.reason: A health check is operational hardening for running at scale; competitors partial.

g-prometheus.reason: Prometheus metrics serve hosting providers running at scale; competitors partial at best.

g-audit.reason: Decided no: the audit log is Nextcloud's admin_audit app.

g-activity.reason: Changes in the activity stream support audit and accountability; no competitor rates yes.

g-cleanup.reason: Cleaning data of deleted users keeps large installations healthy; two competitors have it.

g-cli.reason: Command line management is for hosters and scripted operations at scale; competitors partial.

g-footer.reason: Deferred: partial, built, no demand; one competitor yes.

g-allowlists.reason: Deferred: partial, built, no demand; occ already sets the lists.

g-svg.reason: Removing scripts from uploaded icons is a security baseline before any real organisation uploads files.

p-sso.reason: Table stakes: all five competitors support single sign on with the organisation's identity provider.

p-mobile-app.reason: Decided no: a native app is a recorded non-goal; the mobile browser and PWA cover it.

p-own-servers.reason: Running on own servers is why organisations pick Nextcloud; three competitors allow it.

p-theme.reason: Government organisations need their own colours and NL Design System theming from day one.

p-custom-css.reason: Two homelab competitors rate yes; theming already covers organisational styling.

p-background.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

p-languages.reason: Table stakes: all five competitors are multilingual; Dutch is required.

p-standalone.reason: Installing on a plain Nextcloud without other products is needed for any organisation to adopt it.

p-multitenant.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

d-widget-twice.reason: Three competitors allow the same widget twice; needed for two feeds or two folders.

d-teams.reason: Decided no: no competitor rates yes, outside the core area.

d-account-move.reason: Decided no: no competitor rates yes, outside the core area.

d-link-target.reason: A feature request with two competitors yes; a small preference, not needed to do the job.

d-auto-refresh.reason: Three competitors refresh on their own; a start page left open all day must stay current.

d-idp-groups.reason: Three competitors follow identity provider groups; group dashboards depend on correct groups after sign in.

d-tour.reason: One competitor rates yes; a tour helps onboarding but the wizard covers setup.

d-pwa.reason: Table stakes: all five competitors install on a phone home screen.

d-rest-api.reason: A documented API is an integration demand in tenders; three competitors have it.

d-proxy.reason: Outbound proxy support is required in locked down government networks; three competitors have it.

d-single-logout.reason: Decided no: single logout is done by Nextcloud's login apps.

d-import-bookmarks.reason: A feature request with no competitor yes; tiles can be added by hand.

d-notes.reason: One competitor rates yes; personal notes are an extra, Nextcloud Notes exists.

d-internal-url.reason: One homelab competitor rates yes; split network addresses are a niche need.

d-theme-per-dashboard.reason: Two competitors rate yes; organisation wide theming covers most needs.

d-open-inside.reason: Three competitors rate yes, but opening apps in a pane is convenience over a new tab.

d-search-prefix.reason: Two homelab competitors rate yes; search shortcuts are a power user extra.

d-dark-mode.reason: Table stakes and accessibility: four of five competitors follow the device's dark mode.

d-tile-sort.reason: One competitor rates yes; sorting options are polish.

d-ai-write.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

d-room-free.reason: Decided no: one competitor, no demand, outside the core area.

d-profile-fields.reason: Two competitors rate yes; extra profile fields from the identity provider are intranet extras.

d-news-preview.reason: Previewing news before publishing belongs with announcements, an intranet suite feature for tenders.

d-recurring-events.reason: Decided no: no competitor rates yes, outside the core area.

d-content-review.reason: Decided no: no competitor rates yes, outside the core area.

d-ai-chart.reason: Decided no: no competitor rates yes, outside the core area.

d-work-queue.reason: A tender asks for own cases on the start page; delivered through case app widgets.

w-attention.reason: A ranked list of what needs attention today is daily start page use for case workers.

w-menu.reason: No competitor data and no demand; the organisation menu and tiles cover navigation.

w-quicklinks.reason: No competitor data; tiles and bookmarks already offer shortcuts.

d-public-start.reason: A tender asks for a public start page for signed out visitors; two competitors have it.

d-find-expert.reason: A tender asks to find colleagues by expertise; two intranet competitors have it.

s-embed-site.reason: No competitor data and no demand; embedding on websites is beyond the start page job.

w-calculated-fields.reason: No competitor data and no demand; formulas are analytics extras.

w-map.reason: No competitor data and no demand; a map of register objects is a specialist widget.

q-integrations-gate.reason: Integrations page visibility with integriq belongs with the production integration rows.

q-charts-live.reason: Real figures in chart widgets belong with the reporting rows, which are production.

q-registry-live.reason: Follows r-registry, which has no competitor yes and no demand.

q-groupfolder.reason: A storage backend option in beta with no competitor data or demand.

q-comments.reason: No competitor data and no demand; Talk and the activity stream cover discussion.

q-sibling-widgets.reason: Role scoped widgets from fleet apps are integration work across Conduction apps.

q-person-activity.reason: Reporting one named person's activity raises privacy questions and has no demand row.

q-drive-nc-dashboard.reason: A research task to verify a competitor column, not a capability a customer needs.
